16: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ lie on a circle centered at $O$. Segment $AC$ is a diameter of the circle, and the central angle $AOB$ measures $82^\circ$ (see figure). The measure of angle $OBC$ is equal to: A. $41^\circ$ B. $45^\circ$ C. $49^\circ$ D. $51^\circ$
17: A circle and a line tangent to it at point $A$ are given. Points $B$ and $C$ lie on the circle so that $BC$ is its diameter. Chord $AB$ makes an angle of $40^\circ$ with the tangent (see figure). The measure of angle $ABC$ is equal to: A. $20^\circ$ B. $40^\circ$ C. $45^\circ$ D. $50^\circ$
18: A right triangle $ABC$ has sides $|AC|=24$, $|BC|=10$, $|AB|=26$. The angle bisectors of this triangle meet at point $P$ (see figure). The distance $x$ of point $P$ from the hypotenuse $AB$ is equal to: A. $2$ B. $4$ C. $\frac{5}{2}$ D. $\frac{13}{3}$
19: One of the sides of a parallelogram has length equal to $5$. The diagonals of this parallelogram can have lengths: A. $4$ and $6$ B. $4$ and $3$ C. $10$ and $10$ D. $5$ and $5$
20: In a certain isosceles triangle the largest angle measures $120^\circ$, and the longest side has length $12$ (see figure). The shortest altitude of this triangle has length equal to: A. $6$ B. $2\sqrt{3}$ C. $4\sqrt{3}$ D. $6\sqrt{3}$
22: The lines with equations $y=-\frac{1}{m-2}x-1$ and $y=\frac{1}{3}x+1$ are parallel. It follows that: A. $m=\frac{5}{3}$ B. $m=-1$ C. $m=\frac{7}{3}$ D. $m=5$
23: In rectangle $ABCD$ the vertices $C=(-3,1)$ and $D=(2,1)$ are given. Side $AD$ has length $6$. The area of this rectangle is equal to: A. $6\sqrt{29}$ B. $12\sqrt{2}$ C. $24$ D. $30$
25: A regular prism has $36$ edges. The length of each of these edges is equal to $4$. The lateral surface area of this prism is equal to: A. $176$ B. $192$ C. $224$ D. $288$
26: The slant height (height of a lateral face) of a regular hexagonal pyramid is $2$ times longer than the edge of its base. The ratio of the lateral surface area of this pyramid to the area of its base is equal to: A. $\frac{1}{2}$ B. $\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}$ C. $1$ D. $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$
27: A box contains tiles with letters. Each tile has one printed letter - a consonant or a vowel. There are 25% more tiles with consonants than tiles with vowels. One tile is drawn at random. The probability of drawing a tile with a vowel is equal to: A. $0.75$ B. $0.25$ C. $\frac{4}{9}$ D. $\frac{5}{9}$
28: The arithmetic mean of the four positive numbers $2$, $3x$, $3x+2$, $3x+4$ is equal to $\frac{13}{2}$. It follows that: A. $x=9$ B. $x=\frac{13}{2}$ C. $x=\frac{5}{9}$ D. $x=2$
31: An arithmetic sequence $(a_n)$ is defined for every natural number $n\ge1$. The sum of the first twenty terms of this sequence is equal to $20a_{21}+62$. Calculate the common difference of the sequence $(a_n)$.
32: A trapezoid has bases of lengths $a$ and $b$ and height $h$. Each of the bases of this trapezoid was extended by 25%, and the height was shortened so that a new trapezoid of the same area was formed. Calculate by what percentage the height $h$ of the trapezoid was shortened.
33: In triangle $ABC$, sides $BC$ and $AC$ have equal length. Line $k$ is perpendicular to base $AB$ of this triangle and intersects sides $AB$ and $BC$ at points $D$ and $E$ respectively. The area of quadrilateral $ADEC$ is 17 times greater than the area of triangle $BED$. Calculate $\frac{|CE|}{|EB|}$.
34: From the set of all two-digit natural numbers whose tens digit belongs to the set $\{3,4,5,6,7,8\}$ and whose units digit belongs to the set $\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, one number is drawn at random. Calculate the probability of the event that the drawn two-digit number is divisible by $4$.
35: The base $AB$ of isosceles triangle $ABC$ lies on the line with equation $y=-2x+16$. Vertices $B$ and $C$ have coordinates $B=(3,10)$ and $C=(-2,3)$. Calculate the coordinates of vertex $A$ and the area of triangle $ABC$.
